overview: This 48-page file brings together U.S. wartime investigations and administrative records concerning suspected Japanese espionage, subversion, collaboration, and economic penetration across Latin America, Europe, China, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific. Dating chiefly from 1941–1944, with later routing material from 1947, its contents range from intercepted correspondence and Office of Naval Intelligence memoranda to diplomatic telegrams, case jackets, and cross-references. The largest dossier examines SKF’s multinational operations, alleged pro-Axis personnel, and possible transfers of strategic materials to Japan and Manchukuo, culminating in personnel dismissals in Brazil. Smaller cases concern C. Fujii, Wang Jingwei representative Li Shengwu, Tanji in Tahiti, Ely Widler in China, and Serge Wittouck’s pursuit of Portuguese Timor oil concessions.
interest: Shows US officials assembling fragmentary censorship, naval, diplomatic and corporate intelligence into security cases, notably the SKF dossier.
